glossary.Neoplastic: Caused by abnormal, uncontrolled cell growth (a neoplasm).
glossary.Neoplasm: An abnormal growth of cells; can be benign or malignant.
glossary.Bone marrow: The soft tissue inside bones where blood cells are made.
glossary.Stem cell: An unspecialised cell that can divide and develop into different blood cell types.
glossary.Cell lines: The separate families of blood cells: red cells, white cells and platelets.
glossary.Thrombosis: Formation of a blood clot inside a vessel.
glossary.Constitutional symptoms: Whole-body symptoms such as fever, weight loss, night sweats and fatigue.
glossary.Incidentally: Found by chance while testing for something else.
glossary.Cachexia: Severe wasting of muscle and fat from chronic illness.
glossary.Early satiety: Feeling full after eating only a little, here from a large spleen pressing on the stomach.
glossary.Hb: Haemoglobin, the oxygen-carrying protein in red cells; measured on a full blood count.
glossary.Platelets: Small cell fragments that help blood clot.
glossary.Marrow failure: The bone marrow cannot make enough normal blood cells.
glossary.Stroke: Brain damage from a blocked or burst blood vessel.
glossary.DVT: Deep vein thrombosis: a clot in a deep vein, usually in the leg.
glossary.PE: Pulmonary embolism: a clot blocking an artery in the lungs.
glossary.Hyperviscosity: Abnormally thick blood that flows sluggishly, causing headache, visual upset and clots.
glossary.Acute leukaemia: A fast-growing cancer of immature blood cells in the marrow.
glossary.Giant platelets: Abnormally large platelets on a blood film, typical of ET.
glossary.Syncope: A brief loss of consciousness (a faint).
glossary.Atypical chest pain: Chest pain that does not fit the classic pattern of angina.
glossary.Ischaemic stroke: A stroke caused by a blocked artery cutting off blood to part of the brain.
glossary.Bone marrow aspiration: Drawing liquid marrow through a needle, usually from the hip bone, to examine the cells.
glossary.Anaemia: A low haemoglobin level, so the blood carries less oxygen.
glossary.WCC: White cell count, the number of white blood cells in the blood.
glossary.Blood film: A drop of blood smeared on a slide and looked at under a microscope.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: measures red cells, white cells, platelets and haemoglobin.
glossary.Collagenous matrix: A scaffold of collagen fibres, here the scar tissue replacing normal marrow.
glossary.EPO: Erythropoietin, the kidney hormone that drives red cell production.
glossary.Immature cells: Young blood cells that are normally kept in the marrow until they mature.
glossary.Antiplatelet: A drug that stops platelets sticking together, reducing clots.
glossary.Transfusion: Giving donated blood or blood products into a vein.
glossary.Targeted therapy: Drugs aimed at a specific faulty molecule, such as JAK inhibitors.
glossary.Cytokine: A signalling protein that cells use to tell each other to grow or react.
glossary.Fibroblast: A cell that makes collagen and scar tissue.
glossary.Acute myeloid leukaemia: A fast-growing cancer of the myeloid blood cell line, often arising from other marrow disorders.
glossary.Transformation: Change of a chronic blood disorder into a more aggressive one, such as acute leukaemia.
